div.head: Northu 40
div.ab: Gif preost searwað bewínde, gebete þæt.
Gif preost searwað bewinde, gebete þæt.
Wenn ein Priester mit Trug dies (oder einen Eid?) umgiebt [d. h. sinnwidrig verdreht], büsse er das.
If a priest wraps this (or an oath?) in deceit [i.e. perversely twists it], let him atone for it.
If a priest covers up fraud, he is to compensate for it.
If a priest conceals fraud while conducting an ordeal, he is to atone for that.
div.note: Liebermann thinks ‘searwað’ corrupt and would read ‘searwa þæt’ or ‘searwe að’. Thorpe suggested ‘scearwað’ (tonsure), Ettmüller ‘scearswaðu’, Toller ‘be winde’ (cheats in wrapping [the hand endangered by the ordeal]); Liebermann notes that none of these three words occurs.

conceals fraud while conducting an ordeal: Literally, “If a priest deceives while binding,” presumably a reference to the bandaging of a proband’s burn or wound (so that the healing process may be inspected several days later) in the course of an ordeal.

note.seg: Verderbt; bessere searwa [statt -we] ꝥ [den Haken vergass D auch oben S. 237⁴] oder searwe að. [Scearwað (tonsura) empfiehlt Thorpe; scearswaðu (tonsurae vestigium) Ettmüller Lex. Anglosax. 679; be winde (‘bei Umwindung [der von Ordalhitze gefährdeten Hand] betrügt’) Toller Anglo-Saxon dict. 853. 1231. Aber diese drei Wörter kommen nicht vor].

Corrupt; read searwa [for -we] ꝥ [D also forgot the hook above, p. 237⁴] or searwe að. [Scearwað (tonsura) is recommended by Thorpe; scearswaðu (tonsurae vestigium) Ettmüller Lex. Anglosax. 679; be winde (‘cheats while binding’ [the hand endangered by the heat of the ordeal]) Toller Anglo-Saxon dict. 853. 1231. But these three words do not occur].

Die Bed. ‘umgeben, schützen’ kommt bildlich (‘mit Ruhme, Ehre, Freude, Sorge’: mid seorwe bewunden Stratmann 72) auch sonst vor für bewindan; Toller 97 und Suppl. Dass sich ‘List’ gern mit ‘binden, flechten’ verbindet, beweisen die Composita searubend, -bunden, -sæled, -net. Vgl. Gl Ordal 12. 16a. b

The meaning ‘surround, protect’ also occurs elsewhere for bewindan in a figurative sense (‘with fame, honour, joy, sorrow’: mid seorwe bewunden Stratmann 72); Toller 97 and Suppl. That ‘cunning’ readily combines with ‘binding, weaving’ is proved by the compounds searubend, -bunden, -sæled, -net. Cf. Gl Ordal 12. 16a. b

note.label: fraud
note.seg: Liebermann thought searwað bewinde corrupt, but I take searwað as an unrecorded abstract noun. Bos-worth-Toller reads searwað be winde, rendering it “uses deceit in respect to the wrapping up of the hand”; but wind in this sense is unique.
